messages:
Maria (Support): Escalating ticket from @customer_xyz. They see intermittent failures when calling tools via our OpenAI-compat endpoint. Getting 400s with schema mismatch errors. No billing/auth issues reported. Pasted payload and error below.

customer_xyz: Started failing after we flipped to the compat tool schema. Roughly 30-50% of calls fail with: 400 tool_call_schema_mismatch. We use 'role': 'admin' in our client. Docs on OpenAI-compat we used list ['admin','member','guest'].

Maria (Support): Request body (redacted token):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Body:
{
  "model": "gpt-compat-3.1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"create account"}],
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "user_service.create",
    "arguments": {
      "username": "alpha-test",
      "role": "admin"
    }
  }
}
```

Maria (Support): Error returned by our API: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": {
    "code": "tool_call_schema_mismatch",
    "message": "Argument 'role' not accepted for user_service.create",
    "details": {
      "field": "tool_call.arguments.role",
      "expected_enum": ["admin_user", "regular_user", "guest"]
    }
  }
}
```

customer_xyz: Their SDK docs explicitly used 'admin' — they've been running against an OpenAI-style enum for months. We didn't change the client. This started near the time you rolled changes last night.

Jon (Eng): Can you give the request id and which region/variant it hit? Also need the model variant and any headers.

Maria (Support): request_id: rx-9b4f2c. Routed to hosted-west-2, variant gpt-compat-3.1-fp16. No special headers in the failing sample. I added the observability trace link.

ops-bot: trace: https://observability.redwood/replay/rx-9b4f2c

Sara (ML): Noting we introduced a change in the openai-compat adapter last deploy to prefer canonical enum values. That PR normalized a handful of enums to align with backend service schemas. If legacy aliases were removed it would explain this.

Jon (Eng): Show me the adapter mapping for user_service.create. Also check deploy window and whether this went behind a feature flag.

Maria (Support): Attaching the customer's curl repro (token placeholder):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '@payload.json'

# payload.json is same as above
```

Sara (ML): Found PR 4047 that normalized user roles to the canonical set (admin_user, regular_user, guest). It merged in last night's deploy to hosted-west-2 at 23:40 UTC. The PR message: "openai-compat: normalize role enums to service canonical names".

Jon (Eng): That fits. We need repro showing pre-change behavior. @customer_xyz, can you attempt adding header Accept-Preview: openai_compat=legacy to bypass the new normalization? If that succeeds, we confirm adapter is the problem.

customer_xyz: Trying now. One sec.

customer_xyz: Confirmed — with Accept-Preview: openai_compat=legacy the call returns 200 and tool executed. So translation is the cause.

Maria (Support): Proposed immediate actions: 1) Provide workaround (legacy header) to customer. 2) Engineering: either restore alias mapping or make adapter accept both enum variants. 3) DevEx: update docs & changelog. 4) Add telemetry alert for tool_call_schema_mismatch spikes.

Jon (Eng): I will open a hotfix to re-add alias mapping for user_service.create and add adapter-side tolerant validation so both 'admin' and 'admin_user' accepted. Also add unit tests exercising old compat payloads.

Sara (ML): Also add integration tests that run the entire openai-compat flow with prior enum values to prevent future regressions. And log original arguments (redacted) when mismatch occurs to speed troubleshooting.

Alex (DevEx): I'll draft a migration note and send an in-product banner to customers who use the compat endpoint notifying them of the enum canonicalization change and the header workaround.

Jon (Eng): PR 4079 opened: "compat: reintroduce 'admin' alias for user_service.create and tolerant enum validation". Requesting review from @Sara and @ops.

ops-bot: CI green for PR 4079. Staging deploy scheduled.

Maria (Support): I told customer the workaround and that we expect a hotfix within the hour. They asked for a rollback guarantee if the fix isn't live within 4 hours. I logged that in the ticket.

Jon (Eng): Rolling the hotfix to hosted-west-2 now. Monitoring logs for any spike.

ops-bot: Deploy to hosted-west-2 completed. Canary samples show successful calls. No spike in errors in the last 10 minutes.

Maria (Support): Customer ran their smoke tests and reports success. Marking ticket as mitigated; still keeping it open for follow-up actions (tests/docs/alerting + global deploy).

customer_xyz: Appreciate the quick turnaround, thanks everyone. Please confirm once the global rollout is done and postmortem is published. :pray:

Jon (Eng): Postmortem outline: timeline, root cause (OpenAI-compat enum normalization removed legacy alias), detection (customer report + lack of telemetry rule), remediation (re-add alias + tolerant validation), testing (unit & integration), docs (migration note), and follow-ups (alerting + changelog). Assigning authors: Jon and Alex.

Sara (ML): Adding tests and a telemetry rule to detect >5% tool_call_schema_mismatch rate in any region for 30m.

Alex (DevEx): I'll update the developer migration guide and publish a changelog entry. Also will coordinate a short email to active compat users.

Maria (Support): Moving final conversation + postmortem to #incidents channel. Closing out in support channel. :white_check_mark:
